arxiv-1807-08844.title: Lesion segmentation using U-Net network
arxiv-1807-08844.creator: Adrien Motsch, Sébastien Motsch, Thibaut Saguet
arxiv-1807-08844.description: Abstract This paper explains the method used in the segmentation challenge (Task 1) in the International Skin Imaging Collaboration’s (ISIC) Skin Lesion Analysis Towards Melanoma Detection challenge held in 2018. We have trained a U-Net network to perform the segmentation.

arxiv-2104-07639.title: Robust Optimization for Multilingual Translation with Imbalanced Data
arxiv-2104-07639.creator: Xian Li, Hongyu Gong
arxiv-2104-07639.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Xian Li, Hongyu Gong. Multilingual models are parameter-efficient and especially effective in improving low-resource languages by leveraging crosslingual transfer. Despite recent advance in massive multilingual translation with ever-growing model and data, how to effectively train multilingual models has not been well understood. In this paper, we show that a common situation in multilingual training, data imbalance among languages, poses optimization tension between high resource and low resource languages where the found multilingual solution is often sub-optimal for low resources.

arxiv-2109-12441.title: Accelerated consensus in multi-agent networks via memory of local averages
arxiv-2109-12441.creator: Aditya Bhaskar, Shriya Rangarajan, Vikram Shree, Mark Campbell, Francesca Parise
arxiv-2109-12441.description: Abstract Classical mathematical models of information sharing and updating in multi-agent networks use linear operators. In the paradigmatic DeGroot model, agents update their states with linear combinations of their neighbors’ current states. In prior work, an accelerated averaging model employing the use of memory has been suggested to accelerate convergence to a consensus state for undirected networks.

arxiv-2207-07190.creator: Ata Atay and Christian Trudeau
arxiv-2207-07190.description: Abstract . This paper studies queueing problems with an endogenous number of machines with and without an initial queue, the novelty being that coalitions not only choose how to queue, but also on how many machines. For a given problem, agents can (de)activate as many machines as they want, at a cost.

arxiv-2405-06584.title: How often does a cubic hypersurface have a rational point?
arxiv-2405-06584.creator: Lea Beneish 1, Christopher Keyes 2
arxiv-2405-06584.description: Abstract . A cubic hypersurface in ℙ n \mathbb{P}^{n} defined over ℚ \mathbb{Q} is given by the vanishing locus of a cubic form f f in n + 1 n+1 variables. It is conjectured that when n ≥ 4 n\geq 4 , such cubic hypersurfaces satisfy the Hasse principle.

arxiv-2511-22610.title: Super-resolution of satellite-derived SST data via Generative Adversarial Networks
arxiv-2511-22610.creator: Claudia Fanelli, Tiany Li, Luca Biferale, Bruno Buongiorno Nardelli, Daniele Ciani, Andrea Pisano, Michele Buzzicotti
arxiv-2511-22610.description: Abstract In this work, we address the super-resolution problem of satellite-derived sea surface temperature (SST) using deep generative models. Although standard gap-filling techniques are effective in producing spatially complete datasets, they inherently smooth out fine-scale features that may be critical for a better understanding of the ocean dynamics.

britannica-1911-yeoman.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-yeoman.description: Article 'Yeoman' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 28), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. YEOMAN, a term of which the various meanings fall into two main divisions, first that of a class of holders of land, and secondly that of a retainer, guard, attendant or subordinate officer or official. The word appears in M.E. as ȝeman, ȝoman and yeman; it does not appear in O.E.

pmc-10628091.title: Maternal factors associated with early childhood caries among 3–5-year-old children with low socio-economic status in Trishal, Bangladesh
pmc-10628091.creator: Farzana Haque, Morenike Oluwatoyin Folayan, Jorma Ilmari Virtanen
pmc-10628091.description: IntroductionEarly Childhood Caries (ECC) is more prevalent in nations where a larger portion of the population resides below the poverty line. This study aimed to evaluate the connections between maternal awareness, attitudes, practices related to oral health, and the occurrence of ECC among children aged 3–5 years in Bangladesh, a low–middle income country with high level of poverty.

pmc-11354120.title: No Evidence That Vitamin D Levels or Deficiency Are Associated with the Risk of Open-Angle Glaucoma in Individuals of European Ancestry: A Mendelian Randomisation Analysis
pmc-11354120.creator: Nour Kanso, Munisa Hashimi, Hasnat A Amin, Alexander C Day, Fotios Drenos, Dror Sharon
pmc-11354120.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Glaucoma is the second leading cause of blindness worldwide, with intraocular pressure as the only known modifiable risk factor. Vitamin D has been proposed to influence intraocular pressure and decrease retinal ganglion cell degeneration. Based on these findings, vitamin D has been suggested to prevent or reduce the severity of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), which is the most common form.
